pr_comments:
@elupus When I try image magic, I find that one of the test cases (svg with leading whitespace) is reported as an 'ASCII text' file, which then fails.

The aim is to determine whether the image file is valid too, not just report what the server says it is.
Why cant we just trust the servers content type, if it report some binary format we use magic?

@elupus We are trying to determine whether the server returns a valid image, rather than whether it thinks it returns a valid image.  So if it returns the wrong type or `text/plain` because it has not been configured, then it can still work, as long as there is an image there.
Its not our job to make sure servers are configured properly. We should push fixes to where they are supposed to be. Do you have a example of a server that cant be fixed?

I have been sent some strange image types that made things fail before, and added them all as tests to prevent regression.  But I've no idea what content types were being reported in those cases.

I could update the PR to check that the reported image type matches the detected image type (and warn if not).

Honestly, I have second thoughts about this PR. Which cameras provide SVGs as their still images?

../Frenck

@frenck The issue is described pretty clearly in the linked https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/80802 – they want to use a ([semi-dynamic](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/80802#issuecomment-1288080535)) SVG of their Wifi QR code as a static camera, which sounds reasonable, and this certain form of SVG isn't supported.

@frenck As I understand it, generic cameras already do support SVGs, but only if they had a certain prelude (as per the PR description: "svg still images were rejected if the image file started with `<?xml` rather than `<svg`"), and this PR fixes that to support both preludes.

(Also, what sort of generic component would you use for something that delivers a stream of images if not a generic camera?)

> Also, what sort of generic component would you use for something that delivers a stream of images if not a generic camera?

None. We don't have a construct for that.

We are currently working on a new entity to provide those (but that isn't ready yet; as part of that work, we renamed `image` to `image_upload` in the last release to free up the domain).

The generic camera integration is targeted at IP cameras, but people use it for more than that (e.g. weather maps #68889), where they just want an image based on a URL or URL template.

If there is something in the pipeline that can support SVG directly, support could be taken out of generic and moved to that.  Maybe with a 'repair' to help people with the transition?

> The generic camera integration is targeted at IP cameras, but people use it for more than that 

Sure, but the question was more about this PR itself, as it improves handling of SVG. Hence my question was: For which cameras would that be?

> If there is something in the pipeline

Yes, as per above.

>  that can support SVG directly, support could be taken out of generic and moved to that. Maybe with a 'repair' to help people with the transition?

That is not conclusive at this point. Before creating and discussing things like repairs we have to finish something usable first. One step at a time.

The current [docs](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/generic/) include two examples that are not cameras, one of which is SVG, so I think it's reasonable that people expect SVG to work (which it does mostly) until there's a better option for non-cameras.

A new `image` entity component is implemented in this PR: <https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/90564>
I think support for manually serving an image from a URL could be implemented by adding an `image` component to the `template` integration?

@emontnemery Yes, I agree.

If an image viewer can be made, we don't need this complexity in the generic camera integration.

There will still be cases where a camera serves a still image faster than starting a stream and extracting an image, but I very much expect that to be limited to a small number of file types (perhaps only png and jpeg).

I think the edge cases like SVG are coming from web pages, not cameras.

So yes, your PR would go towards removing the need for this one.

I'll leave this one as draft for now.

@emontnemery Do you know if there is an intention to make the new image entity available to set up from the UI as an integration?

If so I don't think this PR is needed.
I think this is no longer needed due to equivalent functionality being available in #90564

issue_context.title: Generic camera problem with SVG format
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Steps to reproduce:

1.
Create qr code from qrserver, for example this one:
http://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?data=WIFI:T:WPA;S:test;P:test1234;H:;&size=300x300&format=svg

2.
Try to use in generic camera as still image, for example by copying to /config/www/ and using http://192.168.1.2:8123/local/wifi.svg as still image url.

3.
Generic camera throws error as follow:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12937900/197367463-10e469c7-030e-48e2-ac46-dd70d5956204.png)
(tried with ssl verification on and off).

4.
vi the svg and delete the first line.
Try again to use as still image. It now works.

### The error
The created svg file starts with
`<?xml version="1.0" standalone="no"?>`
which IMO is full within standard. It should not cause any error message.

### Workaround
I created a script to always delete the first line of my svg:
 sed -i "1d" /config/www/wifi.svg


### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2022.10.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

generic camera

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/generic/

### Diagnostics information

_No response_

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
camera:
  - platform: generic
    name: wifi password
    still_image_url: http://192.168.1.2:8123/local/wifi.svg
    verify_ssl: false
```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

Confirmed. Can reproduce.  Working on it.

Aside: @cg089 I am curious why you want to use generic camera to display a static image from the local filesystem.  The issue you found was genuine, so thank you for submitting it, but couldn't this have been achieved with a picture card?

Why I don't use a picture card: I have an automamtion to recreate a new guest wifi password every 24 hours. This also recreates the guest wifi qr code which guests will scan on my home assistant.
With a picture card, the new qr code is not being shown after it is recreated. With generic camera and still image, it reloads within seconds: https://community.home-assistant.io/t/updated-automating-unifi-wifi-ssid-password-changes-and-qr-code-generation/

Thanks for your good work and prompt reply!

Ok in that case it sounds like a great use for the generic integration!

Don't know if you realised but you can use templates in the URLs if you want, specifically for this sort of use case.

E.g

`http://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?data={{your-entity-data}}&size=300x300&format=SVG`
